text:
Owen Power, the first pick of the 2021 draft, is 23 and playing like the defenseman Buffalo drafted him to be. He's averaging 25:38 a night, up from 21:39 last season, and he's on the ice for 34% of the Sabres' power-play chances after 12% a year ago. He already has 15 points in 20 games, 0.75 a game against 0.36 last season.

If anything, the luck has run against him. Buffalo has scored 7.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five-on-five the Sabres take 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays, almost 8 points better than when he sits. That usually swings back. Oddly, none of his points have come on the power play yet.

Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern last season: 1.3 expected wins against 0.0 actual, the chances there but not the finish or the saves. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.9 primary shot assists per 60, 96th percentile among defensemen. His goal against Chicago finished a quick passing play from Jack Quinn and Josh Norris. Watch for his power-play time to start turning into points.
headline: Power's breakout is bigger than his points show
